comment: Babb's course is tough. He is very knowledgeable about the subject and will take every opportunity to tell a personal story of his--on topic or not. The class focuses essentially on taking 2 sets of notes--one on his lectures, one on the book. Basically you're taking two separate classes, one on the book & one on his stories. Tests are subjective.

A mixed bag.  Entertaining and outspoken, he’s full of funny anecdotes & tall tales.  Unassuming he’s not, as he’s big-headed & blunt.  While you’ve got to like his confidence & panache, I’m not sure he’s really a great “teacher.”  The project is rough unless you have inspired people in your group.  I’d give Babb a “B, (the same grade he gave me).
Professor Babb has some interesting stories but I learned very little about marketing from his class. Test questions are wordy and unclear.
Most material is from the reading and not discussed in class.

Professor Babb is the best professor I have had in the business school. He applies everything he teaches to the real world. His tests are challenging, but you will learn SO much in his class. You should definitely take his course if you plan to major in Marketing.

Best professor ever. I don't even know what my grade in the class will be and I, honestly, could care less. I felt that I really got a lot out of it and Babb is clearly very knowledgeable. Interesting class.
I did well and liked the class as it is not boring but you have to do A LOT of work outside class to do well.  Tests are super hard but at the end he tends to hand out random A's and stuff.

Hard professor and there is not much structure to the class.  Interesting discussions but often on things that do not appear on the tests.  Tests are very hard and its important to stay up to date in the textbook reading. Trying to cram the night before a test will not work. Gives annoying project.

Great Professor.  I believe one of the best marketing Professors in the country.  His real-world experience and success make all the difference.  He is a venture capitalist currently on his fourth or fifth start-up.  His guidance will take you far, even if you are not interested in marketing.

Class is definitely not an easy A. But Babb is helpful if you go to him outside of class. Tests are a combination of both textbook and lecture. Lectures consist of Babb talking, no powerpoints or writing on the board, about a subject not in the text. So you must be able to take good notes. Textbook is not gone over in class, must read on own.
Arrogant and self-absorbed.  He knows the material, but he cant convey it to students.

Spends more time taking about himself than the material.  There's essentially no work in the course and class is pointless until the tests, which have little to do with what he's taught in class.  Make sure you actually read the book and match it to what he's said as he'll change up terminology on tests between notes and class.  Final projet sucks.

Yawn! We had to do these pointless scholarly articles for review and PLEASE READ the text book in conjunction w/ his notes! Do NOT rely on those notes alone because you will NOT do well! Tests are hard! Assigns this tedious marketing project toward the end of the semester when all other assignments are due! Brags, "I'm so successful!"

extremely entertaining in class. and does a wonderful job of matching you up with a group for your project. you will have a real sense of accomplishment and will really have learned something when you finish this class

Considered dropping class after first test which I did quite poorly on but after that point I knew exactly what I had to do and was able to do it.  Looking back I'm glad I didn't drop the course since it was a valuable experience and Babb is one of the most interesting and down to earth professors at Richmond.
He loves himself.  Really, really loves himself.
Great teacher with enthusiasm and experience in the subject.  Tests are really tough, but you learn a lot.  Recommended for marketing majors. Tales of his own experience make it really cool.
always talking about his life and his stories but never about how hard the exam will be. STUDY Like HELL or YOu will fail his class

A great teacher - I wish he taught more upper level marketing classes! He has great stories, I really enjoyed the class, and although his tests are hard, he still gives plenty of As (even if you didn't always earn it). Participation and a good attitude is key - such a nice guy.
Kind of a fun guy to listen to talk...he has great stories...but his tests suck and the project is a lot of work
